title: fix(turning): Facing, Profile Rough and Profile Finish take a start and an exit pick
body:
Slice 1 of #3331: Facing, Profile Rough and Profile Finish. This PR does not close the issue. The eight other turning kinds are the next slices.

## Review fixes

Head: `449c54fd935d9dd7a6b0d800b6664542bd26ed70`.
Base: `upstream/main` at `baad348f191a5f2261dc778ac3f9853aaf19ffa0`.

- Both `.map_err(&refuse)` calls now use `.map_err(refuse)`.
- The branch includes a merge of current upstream main. The conflict resolutions keep both independent changes.
- `PickCapability::takes` keeps the upstream wire exit support and the new turning capability.
- The MCP description and the shared capability test keep the wire and turning changes.
- A second upstream refresh retains the new Slot `Ends` capability and the turning capability. The shared test keeps both assertions.
- The second refresh does not change the turning controls shown in the screenshots.
- The screenshots below show the old groups and the new turning controls.

## What changed

- A turning pick is a point in the lathe (Z, X) plane. It is a model point `[x, y, z]`. The planner reads it as (station, radius) about the fitted turning axis.
- Start: one rapid goes from the opening point of the path to the pick. The first feed starts at the pick and ends where it ended before.
- Exit: one feed goes from the end of the last feed to the pick. One rapid goes from the pick to the old end point of the path.
- The moves between the first feed and the last feed do not change.
- New module `crates/motion/src/turning/start_exit.rs` (`with_picks`, `PickLaw`). It works on the finished path of a kernel. The kernels do not change.
- The registry has a new capability, `PickCapability::Meridian`, for the three kinds.
- Threading says "not taken" with its own reason: "the thread start law sets the start and the exit of a thread". The G76 start judge does not change.
- MCP: the `edit_operation` schema names the three kinds and says that z is necessary. `list_operation_types` gives `start_exit.plane` for them.
- UI: the Geometry tab of the three kinds has a Start point group and an Exit point group. The rows are typed (Z and X). Apply uses `EditOperationParams`.

A pick is refused by name, and is never moved, when one of these is true:

- The pick has no Z (refused at the command door, with the name of the kind).
- The pick is not in air: it is inside the stock radius and behind the free end, each grown by the nose radius.
- The pick is on the chuck side of the bar.
- The rapid to the start, or the rapid from the exit, crosses the stock envelope.
- The feed between the pick and the cut comes nearer to the part than nose radius + stock to leave - tolerance.
- The exit feed runs along the surface that the last pass cut.
- The path has canned cycles or control compensation.

## Cause

The turning kinds had the `picks` field of #3339, but no planner read it. The registry gave each turning kind the "owed" reason, so the command door refused each pick.

## Where the issue is silent

- The issue does not say how the tool gets from the pick to the first pass. I chose the smallest change: the first feed of the kernel starts at the pick. The kernel ladder does not change.
- The issue does not say which stock a rapid must miss. I chose the envelope of the part and the setup stock. It does not follow stock that earlier operations removed. This is the safe side.
- The issue does not ask for a viewport pick. A turning point is in air, so the wall snap of the 2D Contour pick is not correct for it. The rows are typed.
- The decision file is `docs/decisions/3331-turning-start-exit.md`.

## Tests

Pinning tests:

- `crates/app/tests/start_exit_shared/turning.rs` (8 tests, in the existing `start_exit_shared` binary):
  - `the_first_pass_starts_at_the_start_pick`
  - `the_last_pass_leaves_at_the_exit_pick`
  - `a_start_and_an_exit_pick_hold_together`
  - `an_impossible_pick_is_refused_by_name`
  - `a_pick_whose_move_crosses_the_part_or_the_stock_is_refused_by_name`
  - `threading_keeps_its_start_law_and_says_so_by_name`
  - `undo_and_redo_restore_the_path`
  - `mcp_edit_operation_sets_the_turning_picks_and_undo_clears_them`
- `crates/motion/src/turning/start_exit_tests.rs` (8 unit tests, `turning::start_exit::tests::*`).
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/turning_start_exit_tests.rs` (4 tests, `egui_app::turning_start_exit_rows::tests::*`).
- `every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick` now includes the new capability (an expected change of a pinned list).

Original implementation pin proof: each guard was removed, the pin failed, and the guard was restored.

| Guard removed | Result | Red test |
|---|---|---|
| `generate.rs` of `upstream/main` (no pick laid) | red | 6 of the 8 app tests: `the_first_pass_starts_at_the_start_pick`, `the_last_pass_leaves_at_the_exit_pick`, `a_start_and_an_exit_pick_hold_together`, `an_impossible_pick_is_refused_by_name`, `a_pick_whose_move_crosses_the_part_or_the_stock_is_refused_by_name`, `undo_and_redo_restore_the_path` |
| the "needs a Z" door in `pick_kinds.rs` | red | `mcp_edit_operation_sets_the_turning_picks_and_undo_clears_them` |
| the Threading reason | red | `threading_keeps_its_start_law_and_says_so_by_name` |
| the early return for no pick | red | `no_pick_gives_the_path_back_unchanged` |
| the in-air law | red | `each_law_refuses_by_name` |
| start rapid crosses the stock | red | `a_rapid_through_the_bar_is_refused_by_name` |
| start feed clearance | red | `each_law_refuses_by_name` |
| exit feed clearance | red | `each_law_refuses_by_name` |
| exit lift law | red | `each_law_refuses_by_name` |
| canned cycle / compensation guard | red | `a_path_with_a_canned_cycle_takes_no_pick` |
| arc pass kept whole | red | `an_arc_pass_stays_whole` |
| all guards put back | green | - |

## Final verification

Final head: `449c54fd935d9dd7a6b0d800b6664542bd26ed70`.
Current base: `upstream/main` at `baad348f191a5f2261dc778ac3f9853aaf19ffa0`.
The final commands use this commit as a fixed base. It is the same upstream base used for the final refresh.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base baad348f191a5f2261dc778ac3f9853aaf19ffa0`: 234 steps; 233 passed, 1 failed, 0 stalled. Duration: 23.3 minutes.
- All motion and app steps passed. The motion library had 673 passed and 22 ignored. The app library had 311 passed.
- Only `ui suites: lib` failed: 1664 passed, 7 failed, 8 ignored. These are the same seven no-adapter failures documented in the latest review.
- All four turning UI pinning tests passed. All 12 `start_exit_shared` tests passed, including the shared capability test.

- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed on the final head in 56.16 seconds.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base baad348f191a5f2261dc778ac3f9853aaf19ffa0 --only 'motion heavy: lib' --only 'app heavy: lathe_field_sim' --only 'app heavy: lathe_workholding_kinds' --only 'app heavy: start_exit_shared'`: 4 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. Duration: 3.0 minutes.
- Selected heavy step times: motion library 72 seconds; lathe field simulation 72 seconds; lathe workholding kinds 24 seconds; shared start/exit 2 seconds.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. Duration: 5.5 minutes.

This review round's mutation proof ran on earlier head `a966f17eb988532d0637f0f2f6c80c21c894dc8f`:

| Mutation | Pin | RED result | Restored result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Restore both `.map_err(&refuse)` calls | Motion library clippy with `-D warnings` | Two `needless_borrows_for_generic_args` failures at lines 84 and 113 | Motion library clippy passed |
| Remove upstream Threading exit acceptance | `every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick` | The shared capability test failed | All 12 `start_exit_shared` tests passed |
| Remove Meridian exit acceptance | `every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick` | The shared capability test failed | All 12 `start_exit_shared` tests passed |

Each mutation was restored before the earlier quick gate. These fixes are unchanged on the final head.
The final shared capability test and all 12 tests in its suite passed, as stated above.

## Goldens moved

None in the PR diff against `baad348f191a5f2261dc778ac3f9853aaf19ffa0`. No recorded program or golden file moved in that diff.
Upstream merge commits can contain unrelated golden changes.

Command: `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog --test example_catalog_adaptive --test example_catalog_edge_work --test golden_cl --test lathe_cycle_exit --test lathe_post --test lathe_post_css --test lathe_post_inch --test lathe_post_tormach`. Exit code: 0.

These nine catalog and golden suites passed on final head `449c54fd935d9dd7a6b0d800b6664542bd26ed70`:

| Suite | Passed | Ignored |
|---|---:|---:|
| `example_catalog` | 43 | 4 |
| `example_catalog_adaptive` | 1 | 0 |
| `example_catalog_edge_work` | 1 | 0 |
| `golden_cl` | 34 | 0 |
| `lathe_cycle_exit` | 6 | 0 |
| `lathe_post` | 7 | 0 |
| `lathe_post_css` | 10 | 0 |
| `lathe_post_inch` | 6 | 0 |
| `lathe_post_tormach` | 8 | 0 |

`with_picks` returns the path before it reads a number when there is no pick. `no_pick_gives_the_path_back_unchanged` pins this.

## Screenshots

These images show the real Facing Geometry page through the existing `egui_kittest` page harness.
A temporary software renderer drew the actual egui meshes and font textures. No GPU rendering was validated.
The before capture selected the prior `NotTaken(PICK_OWED)` capability and omitted the new turning group call.
The after captures use the final controls. The second upstream refresh leaves these controls unchanged.
The capture source was restored after both runs passed.
Only the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch contains these images.
The links name immutable image commit `e4452a337c430060533628776372d2f45dd75e42`.

Before: the planner chooses the start and exit.

![Facing Geometry before the turning controls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/e4452a337c430060533628776372d2f45dd75e42/3981/before.png)

After: both points are off by default.

![Facing Geometry with both point controls off](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/e4452a337c430060533628776372d2f45dd75e42/3981/after-default.png)

After: both points are stated. The Start Z/X and Exit Z/X rows are visible.

![Facing Geometry with Start Z/X and Exit Z/X rows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/e4452a337c430060533628776372d2f45dd75e42/3981/after-stated.png)

## Not exercised

The host has no available graphics adapter. The UI library reports `No adapter found` and `no graphics adapter`.
The latest review confirmed the same seven failures on bare upstream main. They are environmental failures.

The full heavy dry run planned 109 steps: 108 reached steps and one build step.
The four selected steps passed on the final head. The remaining full-plan steps did not run.

- Actual GPU rendering. The page screenshots use software rendering of egui meshes.
- The posted G-code text of a program with a pick. The tests read the toolpath moves. The posts read the same moves.
- A turning axis that is not on the model origin, and a lathe with a sub-spindle.
- The exit feed against stock that the operation did not cut. The law checks the part and its stock to leave only. The decision file says this.
- The eight other turning kinds. They keep the "owed" row.

New test files: the app tests are a submodule of the existing `start_exit_shared` binary. No new top-level test binary.

Effort: high

Changelog: Turning: Facing, Profile Rough and Profile Finish take a start point and an exit point in the lathe (Z, X) plane; a point that the laws cannot hold is refused by name.

Refs #3331
